rules.rule_name: Sequential Processing of All Daily Transactions
rules.rule_description: The program reads all daily transaction records one at a time from the Daily Transaction File in sequential order, continuing until all records have been processed.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Daily Transaction File (DALYTRAN-FILE) is open and contains one or more transaction records, and the end-of-file indicator is set to 'N'
acceptance_criteria.When: The program requests the next sequential record from the Daily Transaction File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The next Daily Transaction Record is read into memory, including the Card Number (DALYTRAN-CARD-NUM) and Transaction ID (DALYTRAN-ID), and processing continues for that record

rules.rule_name: End-of-File Detection on Daily Transaction File
rules.rule_description: When the Daily Transaction File has no more records to process, the program detects the end-of-file condition and stops the transaction processing loop.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program is reading records sequentially from the Daily Transaction File
acceptance_criteria.When: A read attempt returns an end-of-file condition (file status '10')
acceptance_criteria.Then: The end-of-daily-transaction-file indicator is set to 'Y', the processing loop terminates, and the program proceeds to close all files

rules.rule_name: Display of Each Transaction Record Upon Successful Read
rules.rule_description: Each successfully read daily transaction record is displayed in full before any validation is performed, providing a log of all transactions encountered.

acceptance_criteria.Given: A daily transaction record has been successfully read from the Daily Transaction File and the end-of-file indicator remains 'N'
acceptance_criteria.When: The record is confirmed as a valid read (not end-of-file)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The full contents of the Daily Transaction Record (DALYTRAN-RECORD) are displayed, including all transaction details

rules.rule_name: Card Number Verification via Cross-Reference File
rules.rule_description: Every transaction's card number must be verified by performing a keyed lookup in the Card Cross-Reference File to confirm the card is known and to retrieve the associated Account ID and Customer ID.

acceptance_criteria.Given: A daily transaction record has been read and its Card Number (DALYTRAN-CARD-NUM) is available
acceptance_criteria.When: The Card Number is used as the key to look up a matching record in the Card Cross-Reference File (XREF-FILE)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If found, the Cross-Reference record is retrieved containing the Card Number (XREF-CARD-NUM), Account ID (XREF-ACCT-ID), and Customer ID (XREF-CUST-ID), and these details are displayed; the cross-reference read status is set to success (0)

rules.rule_name: Transaction Skipped When Card Number Cannot Be Verified
rules.rule_description: If a transaction's card number is not found in the Card Cross-Reference File, the transaction cannot be validated and must be skipped entirely, with a warning logged identifying the unverifiable card and the skipped transaction.

acceptance_criteria.Given: A daily transaction record has been read with a Card Number (DALYTRAN-CARD-NUM) and Transaction ID (DALYTRAN-ID)
acceptance_criteria.When: The Card Number lookup in the Cross-Reference File returns an invalid key (card number not found), setting the cross-reference read status to a non-zero value (4)
acceptance_criteria.Then: A warning message is logged stating 'CARD NUMBER [DALYTRAN-CARD-NUM] COULD NOT BE VERIFIED. SKIPPING TRANSACTION ID-[DALYTRAN-ID]', the transaction is not processed further, and the program moves on to the next transaction record

rules.rule_name: Account Record Retrieval Using Account ID from Cross-Reference
rules.rule_description: When a card number is successfully verified through the Cross-Reference File, the associated Account ID is used to retrieve the full account record from the Account File.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Card Number has been successfully verified in the Cross-Reference File and the Account ID (XREF-ACCT-ID) has been retrieved
acceptance_criteria.When: The Account ID is used as the key to perform a keyed lookup in the Account File (ACCOUNT-FILE)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the account exists, the full Account Record is retrieved and a success message 'SUCCESSFUL READ OF ACCOUNT FILE' is displayed; the account read status is set to success (0)

rules.rule_name: Account Not Found Warning After Verified Card Lookup
rules.rule_description: If the Account ID retrieved from the Cross-Reference File does not correspond to any existing account in the Account File, a warning is issued identifying the missing account.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The card number was successfully verified in the Cross-Reference File and an Account ID (ACCT-ID) was retrieved
acceptance_criteria.When: The keyed lookup of the Account ID in the Account File returns an invalid key (account not found), setting the account read status to a non-zero value (4)
acceptance_criteria.Then: A warning message 'ACCOUNT [ACCT-ID] NOT FOUND' is displayed, and the program continues to process the next transaction record without further processing of the current transaction

rules.rule_name: Program Initialization - Open All Required Files
rules.rule_description: Before any transaction processing begins, all six required files must be successfully opened: Daily Transaction File, Customer File, Card Cross-Reference File, Card File, Account File, and Transaction File.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program CBTRN01C is starting execution
acceptance_criteria.When: The program initializes and attempts to open all required files in sequence: Daily Transaction File (DALYTRAN-FILE), Customer File (CUSTOMER-FILE), Card Cross-Reference File (XREF-FILE), Card File (CARD-FILE), Account File (ACCOUNT-FILE), and Transaction File (TRANSACT-FILE)
acceptance_criteria.Then: All six files are successfully opened and available for processing; if any file fails to open, the program halts immediately with an error message identifying the specific file that could not be opened

rules.rule_name: Program Finalization - Close All Files After Processing
rules.rule_description: After all daily transaction records have been processed (end-of-file reached), all six files must be properly closed in sequence before the program ends.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The end-of-file condition has been detected on the Daily Transaction File and the processing loop has ended
acceptance_criteria.When: The program proceeds to finalize by closing all files in sequence: Daily Transaction File (DALYTRAN-FILE), Customer File (CUSTOMER-FILE), Card Cross-Reference File (XREF-FILE), Card File (CARD-FILE), Account File (ACCOUNT-FILE), and Transaction File (TRANSACT-FILE)
acceptance_criteria.Then: All six files are successfully closed; if any file fails to close, an error message identifying the specific file is displayed, and the program halts; upon successful closure of all files, the program ends normally

rules.rule_name: Daily Transaction File Must Be Available at Program Start
rules.rule_description: The program must successfully open the Daily Transaction File as the first step of initialization. If the file is unavailable, the program cannot continue and must stop immediately.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program CBTRN01C is starting its initialization sequence
acceptance_criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Daily Transaction File for reading
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Daily Transaction File opens successfully, the program proceeds to open the Customer File. If the Daily Transaction File is unavailable or cannot be opened, the program logs an error message 'ERROR OPENING DAILY TRANSACTION FILE', displays the file status details, and terminates immediately without processing any transactions.

rules.rule_name: Customer File Must Be Available at Program Start
rules.rule_description: After successfully opening the Daily Transaction File, the program must successfully open the Customer File. If the Customer File is unavailable, the program cannot continue and must stop immediately.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Daily Transaction File has been successfully opened
acceptance_criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Customer File for reading
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Customer File opens successfully, the program proceeds to open the Card Cross-Reference File. If the Customer File is unavailable or cannot be opened, the program logs an error message 'ERROR OPENING CUSTOMER FILE', displays the file status details, and terminates immediately without processing any transactions.

rules.rule_name: Card Cross-Reference File Must Be Available at Program Start
rules.rule_description: After successfully opening the Customer File, the program must successfully open the Card Cross-Reference File. This file is critical for linking card numbers to accounts and customers. If unavailable, the program cannot continue.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Daily Transaction File and Customer File have both been successfully opened
acceptance_criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Card Cross-Reference File for reading
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Card Cross-Reference File opens successfully, the program proceeds to open the Card File. If the Card Cross-Reference File is unavailable or cannot be opened, the program logs an error message 'ERROR OPENING CROSS REF FILE', displays the file status details, and terminates immediately without processing any transactions.

rules.rule_name: Card File Must Be Available at Program Start
rules.rule_description: After successfully opening the Card Cross-Reference File, the program must successfully open the Card File. If the Card File is unavailable, the program cannot continue and must stop immediately.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Daily Transaction File, Customer File, and Card Cross-Reference File have all been successfully opened
acceptance_criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Card File for reading
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Card File opens successfully, the program proceeds to open the Account File. If the Card File is unavailable or cannot be opened, the program logs an error message 'ERROR OPENING CARD FILE', displays the file status details, and terminates immediately without processing any transactions.

rules.rule_name: Account File Must Be Available at Program Start
rules.rule_description: After successfully opening the Card File, the program must successfully open the Account File. This file is required to validate account details linked to card transactions. If unavailable, the program cannot continue.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Daily Transaction File, Customer File, Card Cross-Reference File, and Card File have all been successfully opened
acceptance_criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Account File for reading
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Account File opens successfully, the program proceeds to open the Transaction File. If the Account File is unavailable or cannot be opened, the program logs an error message 'ERROR OPENING ACCOUNT FILE', displays the file status details, and terminates immediately without processing any transactions.

rules.rule_name: Transaction File Must Be Available at Program Start
rules.rule_description: After successfully opening the Account File, the program must successfully open the Transaction File as the final step of initialization. If unavailable, the program cannot continue and must stop immediately.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Daily Transaction File, Customer File, Card Cross-Reference File, Card File, and Account File have all been successfully opened
acceptance_criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Transaction File for reading
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Transaction File opens successfully, all six required files are available and the program is ready to begin processing daily transactions. If the Transaction File is unavailable or cannot be opened, the program logs an error message 'ERROR OPENING TRANSACTION FILE', displays the file status details, and terminates immediately without processing any transactions.

rules.rule_name: All Required Files Must Be Successfully Opened Before Transaction Processing Begins
rules.rule_description: All six required business files — Daily Transaction File, Customer File, Card Cross-Reference File, Card File, Account File, and Transaction File — must be successfully opened in sequence before any transaction processing can begin. Failure to open any single file prevents the entire program from running.

acceptance_criteria.Then: Only when all six files are opened successfully does the program proceed to transaction processing. rules.rule_name: Search Card Number in Cross-Reference File

rules.rule_name: Determine if Card Number Exists in Cross-Reference File
rules.rule_description: After searching the Cross-Reference File, the system must evaluate whether the card number was found. This decision determines whether the transaction proceeds to account retrieval or is skipped entirely.

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Account ID and Customer ID from Cross-Reference Record
rules.rule_description: When a card number is successfully verified in the Cross-Reference File, the system retrieves the associated Account ID and Customer ID from the matched Cross-Reference record, enabling subsequent account validation.

rules.rule_name: Log Card Number Verification Failure Message

rules.rule_name: Log Skipped Transaction ID When Card Cannot Be Verified

rules.rule_description: The Account ID used to retrieve account details must always be the one obtained from a successful Cross-Reference lookup. Account retrieval is only triggered when the Cross-Reference lookup has succeeded.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Use Account ID obtained from Cross-Reference Lookup

acceptance_criteria.Given: A daily transaction has been read and its card number has been successfully verified through the Cross-Reference file, yielding a valid Account ID
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to retrieve account details
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Account ID obtained from the Cross-Reference record must be used as the key to look up the account, and no account lookup should be attempted unless the Cross-Reference lookup was successful

rules.rule_name: Account Record Lookup Using Account ID as Search Key

rules.sub_graph_node_text: Search Account File Using Account ID as Key

acceptance_criteria.Given: A valid Account ID has been obtained from the Cross-Reference file for a given card number
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs a keyed lookup on the Account File using the Account ID
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must search the Account File using the Account ID as the unique search key to locate the matching account record

rules.rule_name: Successful Account Record Retrieval
rules.rule_description: When the Account File lookup finds a matching record for the given Account ID, the full account details are retrieved and made available for further processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Retrieve Account Details into Account Record

acceptance_criteria.Given: A keyed lookup has been performed on the Account File using a valid Account ID
acceptance_criteria.When: The Account File contains a record matching the provided Account ID
acceptance_criteria.Then: The account details are successfully retrieved into the Account Record and the system confirms successful retrieval of the account

rules.rule_name: Account Not Found for Given Account ID
rules.rule_description: When the Account File does not contain a record matching the Account ID obtained from the Cross-Reference lookup, the system must flag this as an unresolved account and display a warning identifying the missing Account ID.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display: Account Not Found for Account ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: A keyed lookup has been performed on the Account File using an Account ID obtained from the Cross-Reference file
acceptance_criteria.When: No matching account record is found in the Account File for the given Account ID
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must display a warning message stating 'ACCOUNT [Account ID] NOT FOUND', identifying the specific Account ID that could not be located, and continue processing the remaining daily transactions without stopping

rules.rule_name: Account ID Must Be Sourced from Cross-Reference Lookup
rules.rule_description: The Account ID used to search the Account File must be the one retrieved from the Card Cross-Reference record, ensuring the account lookup is always driven by the verified card-to-account mapping.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Use Account ID obtained from Cross-Reference Lookup

acceptance_criteria.Given: A daily transaction has been processed through the Card Cross-Reference lookup and a valid Cross-Reference record has been found containing an Account ID linked to the transaction's card number
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to validate the account associated with the transaction
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Account ID retrieved from the Cross-Reference record (XREF-ACCT-ID) must be used as the key to search the Account File, and no other source of Account ID is permitted for this lookup

rules.rule_name: Account File Must Be Searched Using the Cross-Reference Account ID
rules.rule_description: The system must perform a direct keyed lookup against the Account File using the Account ID obtained from the Cross-Reference record to determine whether the account exists and retrieve its details.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Search Account File using Account ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account ID has been obtained from the Cross-Reference record and is ready for account validation
acceptance_criteria.When: The system searches the Account File using the Account ID as the search key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must perform a direct keyed search of the Account File using the Account ID, and the result must indicate either that the account record was successfully found and retrieved, or that no matching account exists for the given Account ID

rules.rule_name: Valid Account Record Must Be Retrieved When Account Exists
rules.rule_description: When the Account ID is found in the Account File, the full account record must be successfully retrieved and made available for further transaction processing.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has searched the Account File using the Account ID obtained from the Cross-Reference record
acceptance_criteria.When: The Account ID is found in the Account File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The full account record is successfully retrieved into the Account Record, the account read status remains at its initial successful state, and processing continues normally for the transaction

rules.rule_name: Transaction With Unresolvable Account Must Be Flagged
rules.rule_description: When the Account ID obtained from the Cross-Reference lookup does not match any record in the Account File, the system must flag the transaction by displaying an account-not-found message, and then continue processing the remaining transactions without stopping.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has searched the Account File using the Account ID obtained from the Cross-Reference record, and the card number was previously verified successfully through the Cross-Reference lookup
acceptance_criteria.When: The Account ID is not found in the Account File, resulting in a failed account lookup
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must display the message 'ACCOUNT [Account ID] NOT FOUND' identifying the specific Account ID that could not be located, and then return to the transaction processing loop to continue processing the next daily transaction without terminating the program

rules.rule_name: Card Number Must Exist in Cross-Reference File for Transaction Processing
rules.rule_description: Every daily transaction card number must be validated against the Card Cross-Reference File before any further processing can occur. The card number from the daily transaction record is used as the lookup key.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Was Card Number Found in Cross-Reference File?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A daily transaction record has been read from the Daily Transaction File, and the transaction contains a Card Number
acceptance_criteria.When: The Card Number from the daily transaction is looked up in the Card Cross-Reference File using the Card Number as the search key
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Card Number is found in the Cross-Reference File, the transaction is marked as verified and processing continues to Account lookup; if the Card Number is NOT found in the Cross-Reference File, the transaction is marked as unverified and must be skipped

rules.rule_name: Log Warning Message When Card Number Cannot Be Verified
rules.rule_description: When a card number from a daily transaction cannot be found in the Card Cross-Reference File, a warning message must be logged identifying the specific card number that failed verification.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Log Message: Card Number Could Not Be Verified

acceptance_criteria.Given: A daily transaction record has been read and its Card Number has been looked up in the Card Cross-Reference File
acceptance_criteria.When: The Card Number is NOT found in the Card Cross-Reference File (card verification fails)
acceptance_criteria.Then: A warning message is logged stating 'CARD NUMBER [Card Number] COULD NOT BE VERIFIED. SKIPPING TRANSACTION ID-[Transaction ID]', identifying both the unverified card number and the transaction ID being skipped

rules.rule_name: Log Skipped Transaction ID for Unverified Card Transactions
rules.rule_description: When a transaction is skipped due to an unverified card number, the Transaction ID of the skipped transaction must be recorded in the log message to provide a complete audit trail of which transactions were not processed.

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card number from a daily transaction has failed verification against the Card Cross-Reference File
acceptance_criteria.When: The warning message for the unverified card is being logged
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction ID (DALYTRAN-ID) of the skipped transaction is included in the log message alongside the unverified Card Number, so that the specific skipped transaction can be identified for review

rules.rule_name: Skip Transaction and Proceed to Next Record When Card Cannot Be Verified
rules.rule_description: A daily transaction whose card number cannot be verified in the Cross-Reference File must be entirely skipped — no account lookup or further processing is performed — and the program must move on to process the next transaction in the Daily Transaction File.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Skip Transaction Proceed to Next Record

acceptance_criteria.Given: A daily transaction record has been read, its Card Number has been looked up in the Card Cross-Reference File, and the Card Number was NOT found
acceptance_criteria.When: The card verification failure is confirmed and the warning message has been logged
acceptance_criteria.Then: All further processing for that transaction (including Account lookup) is bypassed entirely, and the program proceeds to read and process the next record from the Daily Transaction File without any account or customer updates for the skipped transaction

rules.rule_name: Continue to Account Processing When Card Is Successfully Verified
rules.rule_description: When a card number from a daily transaction is successfully found and verified in the Card Cross-Reference File, the transaction is eligible for further processing, and the Account ID linked to that card is used to look up the full account details.

acceptance_criteria.Given: A daily transaction record has been read and its Card Number has been looked up in the Card Cross-Reference File
acceptance_criteria.When: The Card Number IS found in the Card Cross-Reference File (card verification succeeds), and the Cross-Reference record returns the linked Account ID and Customer ID
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Account ID retrieved from the Cross-Reference record is used to look up the account in the Account File, and processing continues to the account validation step

rules.rule_name: Transaction Processing Loop Continuation Check
rules.rule_description: At the start of each iteration, the system checks whether all daily transaction records have already been read. If not, the loop continues to fetch and process the next transaction. This governs whether the daily transaction processing cycle should continue or stop.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The daily transaction processing loop is active and the End-of-File flag has been initialized to 'N' indicating there are potentially more daily transaction records to be read
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the End-of-File flag at the beginning of each loop iteration
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the End-of-File flag is 'N', the system proceeds to read the next daily transaction record and continues processing; if the End-of-File flag is 'Y', the system exits the processing loop and proceeds to close all files

rules.rule_name: Read Next Daily Transaction Record
rules.rule_description: When the End-of-File flag indicates more records may exist, the system attempts to retrieve the next daily transaction record from the Daily Transaction file for processing.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The daily transaction processing loop is active and the End-of-File flag is 'N', indicating that more daily transaction records may be available
acceptance_criteria.When: The system attempts to read the next record from the Daily Transaction file
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the read is successful, the daily transaction record is retrieved and made available for further processing including card number verification and account lookup; if the read is unsuccessful due to end of file, the End-of-File flag is set to 'Y'; if the read fails for any other reason, the transaction processing is halted

rules.rule_name: Successful Transaction Record Retrieval
rules.rule_description: After attempting to read a daily transaction record, the system determines whether the read was successful. A successful read means a valid transaction record was retrieved and is ready for card verification and account lookup processing.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has attempted to read the next record from the Daily Transaction file
acceptance_criteria.When: The read operation completes and the result is evaluated
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the read was successful (a valid transaction record was retrieved), the transaction record is displayed and the system proceeds to verify the card number against the Cross-Reference file and look up the associated account; the loop then returns to check the End-of-File flag for the next iteration

rules.rule_name: End-of-File Detection on Daily Transaction File
rules.rule_description: When the system attempts to read a daily transaction record and there are no more records remaining in the Daily Transaction file, the End-of-File condition is detected and the processing loop flag is updated to signal that all transactions have been read.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has attempted to read the next record from the Daily Transaction file
acceptance_criteria.When: The read operation determines that no more records exist in the Daily Transaction file (end of file is reached)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The End-of-File flag is set to 'Y', signaling that all daily transaction records have been read; on the next loop iteration, the End-of-File flag check will evaluate to 'Y' and the processing loop will stop

rules.rule_name: Stop Daily Transaction Processing Loop
rules.rule_description: Once the End-of-File flag is set to 'Y', confirming all daily transaction records have been read and processed, the transaction processing loop terminates and the program proceeds to the file closure phase.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Stop Processing Loop Proceed to Close Files

acceptance_criteria.Given: The End-of-File flag has been set to 'Y' after all records in the Daily Transaction file have been read
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the End-of-File flag at the top of the processing loop
acceptance_criteria.Then: The daily transaction processing loop is exited and the system proceeds to close all open files: Daily Transaction file, Customer file, Cross-Reference file, Card file, Account file, and Transaction file, after which the program ends

rules.rule_name: Display Daily Transaction Record Details
rules.rule_description: When a daily transaction record is successfully read and the end of the daily transaction file has not been reached, the full transaction record details are displayed for visibility and audit purposes.

acceptance_criteria.Given: A daily transaction record has been read from the Daily Transaction File and the end-of-file indicator is 'N' (not yet reached end of file)
acceptance_criteria.When: The transaction record is available for processing
acceptance_criteria.Then: The complete transaction record details (including Card Number and Transaction ID) are displayed

rules.rule_name: Look Up Card Number in Card Cross-Reference File
rules.rule_description: For each daily transaction, the card number from the transaction record is used as a key to perform a direct lookup in the Card Cross-Reference File (XREF-FILE, VSAM KSDS) to verify the card and retrieve associated account and customer information.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Look Up Card Number in Cross-Reference File

acceptance_criteria.Given: A daily transaction record has been read with a Card Number (DALYTRAN-CARD-NUM) and the cross-reference read status is initialized to 0
acceptance_criteria.When: The Card Number from the transaction is used as the key to look up the Card Cross-Reference File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system attempts a keyed read of the Card Cross-Reference File using the Card Number as the lookup key, and the result determines whether the card is verified or not

rules.rule_name: Card Number Not Found in Cross-Reference — Skip Transaction
rules.rule_description: If the card number from the daily transaction cannot be found in the Card Cross-Reference File, the transaction cannot be verified and must be skipped. A warning message is logged identifying the unverifiable card number and the skipped transaction ID.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Log Message: 'Card Number Could Not Be Verified' Skip Transaction ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: A daily transaction record has been read with a Card Number (DALYTRAN-CARD-NUM) and a Transaction ID (DALYTRAN-ID)
acceptance_criteria.When: The Card Number is not found in the Card Cross-Reference File (cross-reference read status is set to 4 — invalid key)
acceptance_criteria.Then: A warning message is displayed stating 'CARD NUMBER [DALYTRAN-CARD-NUM] COULD NOT BE VERIFIED. SKIPPING TRANSACTION ID-[DALYTRAN-ID]', and the transaction is skipped without further processing

rules.rule_name: Card Number Verified — Retrieve Account ID and Customer ID from Cross-Reference
rules.rule_description: When a card number is successfully verified in the Card Cross-Reference File, the associated Account ID and Customer ID are retrieved from the cross-reference record. These details are confirmed and made available for subsequent account validation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Retrieve from Cross-Reference: - Account ID - Customer ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: A daily transaction record has been read with a Card Number (DALYTRAN-CARD-NUM)
acceptance_criteria.When: The Card Number is found in the Card Cross-Reference File (successful keyed read — not invalid key)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system retrieves and displays the verified Card Number (XREF-CARD-NUM), the linked Account ID (XREF-ACCT-ID), and the linked Customer ID (XREF-CUST-ID) from the cross-reference record, and the cross-reference read status remains 0 (successful)

rules.rule_name: Look Up Account Record Using Account ID from Cross-Reference
rules.rule_description: After a card number is successfully verified and the Account ID is retrieved from the Cross-Reference File, the Account ID is used as a key to perform a direct lookup in the Account File (ACCOUNT-FILE, VSAM KSDS) to retrieve the full account record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Look Up Account Record Using Account ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The card number has been verified in the Cross-Reference File and the Account ID (XREF-ACCT-ID) has been retrieved, and the account read status is initialized to 0
acceptance_criteria.When: The Account ID is used as the key to look up the Account File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system attempts a keyed read of the Account File using the Account ID (ACCT-ID) as the lookup key, and the result determines whether the account record is found or not

rules.rule_name: Account Record Not Found — Log Warning
rules.rule_description: If the Account ID retrieved from the Cross-Reference File does not match any record in the Account File, a warning message is logged identifying the missing account. This covers both the immediate invalid key detection during the file read and the subsequent status check.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The card number has been verified and the Account ID (ACCT-ID) has been retrieved from the Cross-Reference File
acceptance_criteria.When: The Account ID is not found in the Account File (invalid key during keyed read, setting account read status to 4), and the account read status is checked and found to be non-zero
acceptance_criteria.Then: A warning message 'INVALID ACCOUNT NUMBER FOUND' is displayed at the time of the failed read, and subsequently 'ACCOUNT [ACCT-ID] NOT FOUND' is displayed; the transaction record processing ends without a valid account record

rules.rule_name: Account Record Successfully Retrieved
rules.rule_description: When the Account ID is found in the Account File, the full account record is successfully retrieved and a confirmation message is displayed. The account read status remains 0, indicating successful retrieval.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The card number has been verified and the Account ID (ACCT-ID) has been retrieved from the Cross-Reference File
acceptance_criteria.When: The Account ID is found in the Account File (successful keyed read — not invalid key)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The full account record (ACCOUNT-RECORD) is successfully retrieved, a message 'SUCCESSFUL READ OF ACCOUNT FILE' is displayed, and the account read status remains 0 (successful), completing the transaction record processing successfully

rules.rule_name: Close Daily Transaction File After Processing
rules.rule_description: Once all daily transactions have been processed, the Daily Transaction File must be closed successfully before proceeding to close remaining files.

acceptance_criteria.Given: All daily transactions have been processed and the program is in the finalization phase
acceptance_criteria.When: The program attempts to close the Daily Transaction File
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the file closes successfully, the program proceeds to close the Customer File. If the file fails to close, processing stops immediately and no further files are closed.

rules.rule_name: Close Customer File After Daily Transaction File
rules.rule_description: After the Daily Transaction File has been successfully closed, the Customer File must be closed before proceeding to close remaining files.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Daily Transaction File has been successfully closed during program finalization
acceptance_criteria.When: The program attempts to close the Customer File
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the file closes successfully, the program proceeds to close the Card Cross-Reference File. If the file fails to close, processing stops immediately and no further files are closed.

rules.rule_name: Close Card Cross-Reference File After Customer File
rules.rule_description: After the Customer File has been successfully closed, the Card Cross-Reference File must be closed before proceeding to close remaining files.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Customer File has been successfully closed during program finalization
acceptance_criteria.When: The program attempts to close the Card Cross-Reference File
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the file closes successfully, the program proceeds to close the Card File. If the file fails to close, processing stops immediately and no further files are closed.

rules.rule_name: Close Card File After Card Cross-Reference File
rules.rule_description: After the Card Cross-Reference File has been successfully closed, the Card File must be closed before proceeding to close remaining files.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Card Cross-Reference File has been successfully closed during program finalization
acceptance_criteria.When: The program attempts to close the Card File
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the file closes successfully, the program proceeds to close the Account File. If the file fails to close, processing stops immediately and no further files are closed.

rules.rule_name: Close Account File After Card File
rules.rule_description: After the Card File has been successfully closed, the Account File must be closed before proceeding to close the final file.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Card File has been successfully closed during program finalization
acceptance_criteria.When: The program attempts to close the Account File
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the file closes successfully, the program proceeds to close the Transaction File. If the file fails to close, processing stops immediately and no further files are closed.

rules.rule_name: Close Transaction File as Final Step
rules.rule_description: After the Account File has been successfully closed, the Transaction File is the last file to be closed, completing the program finalization sequence.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account File has been successfully closed during program finalization
acceptance_criteria.When: The program attempts to close the Transaction File
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the file closes successfully, the program reaches its end and terminates normally. If the file fails to close, processing stops immediately and the program does not complete its normal termination.

rules.rule_name: Sequential File Closure Order Enforcement
rules.rule_description: All six files must be closed in a strict sequential order during program finalization: Daily Transaction File first, followed by Customer File, Card Cross-Reference File, Card File, Account File, and Transaction File last.
